sides.claim: Faced with two extreme camps on consumer AI agents (that they are massively overhyped versus that every consumer-facing company is a short because agents will eat their margins), the creator says both are too extreme but if forced to pick, they…

AI agents make price-shopping and replacing skilled workers (e.g., using AI to edit a podcast instead of a consultant) easy, and if saving money is the core consumer use case for AI, this could have a deflationary impact on the consumer economy at…
The creator says they cannot watch how easy Muse is to use and how fast its downloads have taken off and conclude it won't have a big impact on the consumer economy.
The creator suggests that Muse acting as a layer that decides where consumer spend goes is a massive threat and opportunity for retailers, noting as evidence that Amazon banned Muse.

sides.question: whose-margin-pays
sides.claim: Craneware's customer base of established US hospitals is likely highly resistant to replacing entrenched software systems, making the business unlikely to be disrupted by AI coding tools.

sides.question: whose-margin-pays
sides.claim: The major current use case for consumer AI agents appears to be saving people money, as illustrated by widely retweeted examples of an agent called Muse saving users money on insurance, returns, phone bills, and even getting free food.

sides.question: whose-margin-pays
sides.claim: The creator's market-related takeaway is that Muse (a consumer AI agent) is very bearish for businesses that rely on consumer inertia (OTAs, subscription services, banks, etc.), and the stock market seems to be starting to agree with and catch up…

sides.question: whose-margin-pays
sides.claim: Based on conversations with 'normie' friends (a possibly small/early sample), most people who get access to Muse, including the creator himself, have an early productivity burst that fades off hard as usage falls off a cliff within a few days.
